# Independent audit: paired maximum-depth stability transfer


and (R) are now supplied by the complete proof in
`candidate d494e7e71949ac0b`. I independently read
`candidate ecc8b4db4896dd08` and the entire ordinary
local source `candidate c62d1cc13c75171f`.

This audit verifies the transfer, not a mixed-integer conclusion.

## 1. Affine normalization and compact parameters

The paired family is preserved by every invertible ordinary affine map:
normalizing L^(−T)u scales BOTH thresholds by the same positive factor.
The Jacobian multiplies both cap volumes and body volume equally. The
root note explicitly normalizes the enclosing simplex before choosing
normal neighborhoods, shifts, bounding balls, and compact gaps, so its
constants depend only on d. This order is necessary and is now correct.

For a body and candidate in a common ball of radius R, shifts s≥2R have
paired fraction exactly 1/2, up to a null supporting hyperplane. The
same value occurs at s=2R inside the chosen parameter set; hence ignoring
larger shifts cannot lower the infimum. Joint continuity follows from
volume-null hyperplanes. Compactness gives actual minimizing pairs and
maximizing candidates. The total-variation and slab arguments justify
continuity of maximum paired depth without requiring any chosen
optimizer to move continuously.

## 2. The loss bound applies to each shifted cap separately

The ordinary source's weighted-strip lemma assumes only that an affine
halfspace margin is uniformly within η of λ_i−1/(d+1) on the simplex.
It does NOT require the cut to pass through the selected center. Thus
both margins

    |grad λ_i|[u·(x−y)−s],  |grad λ_i|[u·(x−y)+s]

have missing fractions at most the SAME L_i whenever they lie in the
chosen neighborhood. Averaging the two losses still gives L_i, not 2L_i.
The radial disintegration, facet functional, strip constants, and bound
Lbar≤Γ(1−c/2)τ from the ordinary proof are unchanged.

At a canonical pair (u_i,0,g), both margins equal λ_i−1/(d+1), with
strictly positive sign at vertex i and strictly negative signs at the
other vertices. Continuity on the compact simplex therefore gives the
claimed uniform neighborhood and vertex-isolation properties for both
shifted caps. No cap orientation is assumed globally.

## 3. Exact same-normal paired simplex formula

For a fixed nearby u, put h=u·(v_i−y). The edge intercept fraction toward
vertex j≠i is

    (h∓s)/[u·(v_i−v_j)].

All denominators are positive and depend only on u and the simplex;
all fractions belong to (0,1) because each cap isolates exactly vertex i.
Consequently both cap volumes have the same positive coefficient A_u
multiplying (h−s)^d and (h+s)^d. Their average is at least A_u h^d by
convexity of the dth power. The intermediate through-y cap also isolates
vertex i and obeys the ordinary determinant/AM-GM lower bound
 d^d∏_(j≠i)λ_j(y). This exact step introduces no remainder or factor loss.

## 4. One actual balanced center and all other parameters

The selected barycentrics sum to one. Since 0≤L_i,Lbar≤τ, they differ
from 1/(d+1) by at most τ/[(d+1)Γ]. The stated τ≤Γ/2 and δ≤1/4 put
all barycentrics strictly above δ/(d+1), placing the point inside the
inner simplex and hence inside K. The χ bound places it in the single
common cap-localization neighborhood.

The ordinary finite product expansion gives the same remainder
Bτ², B=2^d/Γ. The balanced linear term and the common loss L_i cancel
exactly, leaving Γ−Lbar−Bτ² for every nearby paired parameter.
For the complement, the proved strict nonzero-shift equality lemma and
the canonical zero-shift classification give a positive attained compact
gap at g. Uniform center continuity preserves half that gap. Removing
at most τ in each cap removes at most τ in their average. The stated
τ≤ρ0/4 makes these far parameters satisfy a stronger lower bound.
Larger shifts equal the already covered endpoint value 1/2.

Dividing by 1−τ gives

    P_K(y)−Γ≥[Γcτ/2−Bτ²]/(1−τ)≥Γcτ/4

under τ≤Γc/(4B). The displayed δ_d makes τ≤dδ satisfy every smallness
condition. The case τ=0 is correctly handled separately.

## 5. Every minimizing enclosing simplex and the global extension

The ordinary enclosing-simplex attainment, facet-centroid contacts, and
nearby-vertex estimates do not depend on the chosen depth functional.
They therefore supply the local relative hypotheses for EVERY minimum
container when K is sufficiently close to a simplex. Paired affine
invariance then transports the bound back without changing its constant.

For the global argument, the maximum-volume-inscribed-simplex
normalization gives the same compact class containing the reference
simplex and bounded by one fixed polytope. Its only simplex member is
the reference simplex. Continuity of paired depth and the now-proved
rigidity (R) give an attained strictly positive gap outside the local
neighborhood. The empty-complement convention is legitimate. On that
complement the missing relative volume is at most one, regardless of
which minimum enclosing simplex is used. Combining this with the local
coefficient gives the claimed finite dimension-only global constant.

No d=2 claim, unsupported equality classification, relative-remainder
limit, or compatibility-preserving mixed affine map enters the proof.
The constant Γc/4 is retained exactly.
